# Summary of Political Manifesto (2024)

This manifesto outlines a vision for comprehensive reform across multiple policy areas.

## Economy
The document proposes careful fiscal management while investing in renewable energy and infrastructure. Key economic policies include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy to support high streets, reforming capital gains tax, increasing banking sector taxation, and expanding apprenticeships. A new industrial strategy would focus on green technology, artificial intelligence, and supporting small businesses through improved access to capital.

## Healthcare and Social Care
Healthcare proposals centre on improving GP access through recruiting 8,000 additional doctors and establishing a seven-day appointment guarantee (24 hours for urgent cases). Mental health receives significant attention, with plans for community hubs and school-based professionals. Cancer treatment guarantees, dental access improvements, and a comprehensive social care reform featuring free personal care and a new National Care Agency are included. Unpaid carers would receive increased allowances and respite guarantees.

## Education
Education reforms include increased per-pupil funding, dedicated mental health professionals in schools, tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, and expanded early years provisions. £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants for adult education, reinstated maintenance grants, and teacher recruitment improvements feature prominently.

## Environment
Environmental commitments include achieving net-zero emissions by 2045, generating 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030, and implementing emergency home insulation programmes. Water company reform would address sewage dumping through stricter regulations and a sewage tax. Tree planting targets of 60 million annually and nature restoration goals aim to double protected areas by 2050.

## Housing
Housing policies target 380,000 new homes annually, including 150,000 social homes. Rental reforms include banning no-fault evictions and creating landlord registers. Leasehold abolition and ground rent caps are proposed alongside local authority powers over second homes.

## Constitutional Reform
Democratic reforms include proportional representation through Single Transferable Vote, lowering voting age to sixteen, House of Lords reform, and capping political donations. Enhanced devolution and a federal structure are proposed, alongside ministerial code legislation.

## International Affairs
Foreign policy emphasises closer European relations through a four-stage approach toward Single Market membership, restored 0.7% international development spending, continued support for international institutions, and maintaining nuclear deterrence while increasing defence spending toward 2.5% of GDP.
